states_and_values.simulation_time: Continuous time variable from 0.0 to 5.0 s

assumptions: Time is continuous, strictly monotonic, and independent of physical plant dynamics.
Event triggers are instantaneous at the defined physical scenario times.
connections: Broadcasts simulation_time and event markers to ReleaseFixtureActuator, GroundConstraintEnforcer, and DataLogger.
physical_subsystems.simulation_intent: Provide the master physical timing reference to trigger boundary condition changes at exact physical scenario times without introducing logical delays.

states_and_values.release_force: Vertical support force applied to the airframe mass

parameters.initial_support_force: Force required to hold the equivalent airframe mass in static equilibrium

algebraic_actions.release_force_update: if LOGIC_EVT_DESCENT_START then release_force = 0, fixture_released = true

assumptions: Release is instantaneous at t=0.0s with no mechanical delay or friction.
The fixture does not impart any lateral or rotational forces.
physical_subsystems.simulation_intent: Simulate the physical removal of the support force to initiate free-fall descent of the airframe mass.

states_and_values.y_s: Vertical displacement of the equivalent airframe mass
states_and_values.v_s: Vertical velocity of the equivalent airframe mass
states_and_values.piston_zdd_out: Vertical acceleration of the equivalent airframe mass

assumptions: The airframe mass is a rigid body constrained to 1D vertical translation.
Gravity is constant and acts uniformly on the mass.
connections: Outputs y_s, v_s, and piston_zdd_out to TireContactDynamics and SensorAndTelemetrySystem.
physical_subsystems.simulation_intent: Model the vertical inertial response of the supported airframe mass under gravity, release forces, and strut reaction loads.

states_and_values.y_u: Vertical displacement of the unsprung wheel mass
states_and_values.v_u: Vertical velocity of the unsprung wheel mass
states_and_values.tire_force: Vertical reaction force generated by the tire

assumptions: Tire carcass acts as a linear spring with no internal damping.
Ground surface is perfectly rigid and does not deform.
connections: Receives y_s from AirframeMassDynamics for relative stroke calculation.
Outputs tire_force to OleoGasSpringDynamics and y_u, v_u to SensorAndTelemetrySystem.
physical_subsystems.simulation_intent: Model the unsprung mass dynamics and pneumatic tire deflection upon ground contact to generate the initial impact load.

states_and_values.ground_height: Vertical position of the runway surface
states_and_values.contact_active: Boolean state indicating ground constraint enforcement

algebraic_actions.constraint_activation: if LOGIC_EVT_TOUCHDOWN then ground_height = runway_elevation, contact_active = true

assumptions: Runway surface is perfectly rigid, flat, and horizontal.
Ground constraint activates instantaneously at the physical scenario time.
physical_subsystems.simulation_intent: Enforce the physical boundary condition of the runway surface to generate the ground impact reaction force.

states_and_values.oleo_compression: Relative displacement of the shock strut sliding joint
states_and_values.strut_force: Total pneumatic spring force generated by the gas chamber

assumptions: Gas spring follows a polytropic compression curve.
No internal gas leakage or fluid aeration occurs during the test.
Strut is fully extended at the start of the simulation.
connections: Receives y_s from AirframeMassDynamics and y_u from TireContactDynamics.
Outputs strut_force to AirframeMassDynamics and TireContactDynamics.
physical_subsystems.simulation_intent: Model the pneumatic spring force and relative stroke of the shock strut to absorb and store impact energy.

states_and_values.damping_force: Force generated by hydraulic fluid displacement

algebraic_actions.damping_calc: damping_force = C_v * oleo_compression_speed + C_v2 * sign(oleo_compression_speed) * oleo_compression_speed^2

assumptions: Damping is purely a function of compression speed.
Hydraulic fluid is incompressible and flows through fixed orifices.
No fluid aeration or cavitation occurs.
connections: Outputs damping_force to OleoGasSpringDynamics to be added to the total strut force.
physical_subsystems.simulation_intent: Model the hydraulic energy dissipation during strut compression and rebound to control the rate of energy absorption.

assumptions: Ideal sensors with no latency, bandwidth limitations, or noise.
Continuous sampling at the simulation step rate.
connections: Receives physical states from AirframeMassDynamics, TireContactDynamics, OleoGasSpringDynamics, and HydraulicDamperDynamics.
physical_subsystems.simulation_intent: Capture and stream physical state variables for continuous monitoring, feedback evaluation, and post-processing.

states_and_values.post_impact_stability: Evaluation of rebound decay and settling

algebraic_actions.metric_extraction: update peaks and metrics based on time-series data
algebraic_actions.marker_recording: record PHYS_EVT_DESCENT_START and PHYS_EVT_TOUCHDOWN at corresponding times

assumptions: Post-processing extracts exact peaks from the continuous time-series data.
Stability is evaluated only after physical trace shows reversal/decay behavior.
physical_subsystems.simulation_intent: Record time-series data, extract safety and constraint metrics, and evaluate post-impact stability and bottoming prevention.

physical_driver_profile.profile_description: Boundary condition changes from supported to free-fall. Physical evidence through release_force dropping to 0, making gravity the sole vertical force on the equivalent mass.
Boundary condition changes from airborne to ground contact constraint. Physical evidence through ground_height activating at 0.0, causing tire_deflection > 0 and applying ground reaction force.
